cells.tense: Right now the lending and the seeing are the same act, and the pen is already moving while it happens.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Pick the one place where your strength and someone's need line up, put what you have there once, then let the week move on without checking whether it worked.
cells.core:
You lend strength where it is needed, and you do it by measure. Because you see which thing matters, the weight lands on that thing and not on the four neighbors that could also use a hand. Seeing what to attend to keeps the help from becoming smearing, and it is why your effort can be spent without being wasted. That is the balance: the help goes somewhere true, and the one giving it is still upright afterward.

What this balance is free to feed next is a heading. Pick the one place where your strength and someone's need actually line up, put what you have there, once, then let the week move on without checking back. The other places will keep. Steering is what the pen is for; the light falls on the thing nearest, you go toward it, and the going is what keeps the light a light instead of a glare.
cells.sheetLine: You see what matters. Let that decide where the strength goes.
cells.verb: lending your strength to whoever needs it, by measure
cells.place: the moment you see which thing matters before you can say why

cells.tense: By the time anyone asks, you will already be carrying the whole thing, and the pen will still not have touched the page.
cells.act: act on the private sense of what is right
cells.ask: Name the next thing you owe — a person, an amount, a day — do that one thing first, and let the count stay open.
cells.core:
Support is running past the moment it belongs to. You are already steadying the person who has not asked, already carrying what has not happened yet, already lending by measure before any measure has been taken around you. Underneath that, a private account runs: who has what, who is owed, whether the share is fair, and the account is doing work the lending should be doing. The scale sits on the support, and whoever you brace for can feel the bracing before they ask.

Let the private sense of right decide one small case before the arithmetic can. Name the next thing you owe — a person, an amount, a day — do that thing, and leave the ledger otherwise open. Fairness does not need the counting; it just needs to be spent on the actual hour you are in. The hand that was holding next week gets its weight back for this one.
cells.sheetLine: The bracing is heavier than the thing you're bracing against.
cells.verb: lending your strength to whoever needs it, by measure
cells.place: the moment you see which thing matters before you can say why

cells.tense: The door was already closing when you turned toward it, and you have been standing at its frame since.
cells.act: engage the hard part on purpose and see what holds
cells.ask: Take the piece of this you have been circling, touch it on purpose, long enough to learn whether it holds, then stop.
cells.core:
Strength is being asked for and is not flowing, in either direction. What used to move stands still at a threshold that is no longer there, and the help you do manage comes out one-sided, small, withheld at the last inch. The place where you usually see what matters has gone quiet; that sense did not fail, it simply has nothing coming in to work on. You keep showing up, and your hands know the way.

What gets you back is friction, not rest. Take the piece you have been circling and touch it on purpose, long enough to learn whether it holds. You are not finishing it, only finding out what your commitment is made of. The hard part is what tests a commitment, and the easy part does not. Some methods need to drop away. The point stays.

cells.tense: The steering has had a hand on it the whole time, and the hand has gone unrecognized even while the course was being set.
cells.act: choose which star to steer by and steer
cells.ask: Next time someone asks what you are working toward, skip the shrug and say which way you are pointed, then go back to the work.
cells.core:
There is a direction in what you do, and the people near you can see you holding it. What is on the record is the shrug — the practice you are just keeping up, the help that is not a big deal, the thing you are headed toward but have not decided about. The heading is real and it is yours, and the account you give of it leaves the hand off the wheel. So the support flows out, and whoever set the course does not get counted.

Stop shrinking what you are pointed at. Next time someone asks what you are working toward, the plain answer is the true one: say which way you are pointed, then stop. No speech, no vow, no proof. A heading told plainly does the rest, and the one holding it gets to keep both the hand and the light.
